# AngelBot release runbook

AngelBot keeps development, desktop E2E, and production update capabilities
separate. A normal local release build creates the supported per-user NSIS
installer without any updater key. The GitHub release workflow is the only path that enables the
updater plugin and creates signed update artifacts.

Early GitHub **Pre-releases** and later stable releases have different evidence
requirements. A clean Windows VM, Authenticode certificate and completed manual
checklist are not prerequisites for an early pre-release; disclose their status
instead. Automated checks, code correctness, permission checks and explicit
publication authorization remain required.

## Repository workflow

- `main` is the default/integration branch (renamed from public `dev` on
  2026-10-26 at the owner's request). Use short-lived `codex/<change>` branches
  and open PRs targeting `main`; do not commit or push directly to it. Community
  contributors can use their own fork/branch names. There is no separate `dev`
  promotion lane. Never reconstruct public `main` from private archive history.
- Commit a complete, buildable change, including its frontend/backend contract,
  tests, migrations and necessary documentation. Do not split coupled changes
  merely to make commits smaller. Run `python scripts/verify.py full` before a
  code checkpoint; automated verification must not need model credentials or user data.
  During implementation, use focused regressions and layer/integration checks
  as described in `AGENTS.md`; passing them does not require a user handoff.
  Documentation/instruction-only work may use its documented local checks instead
  of an app rebuild; this does not waive any PR merge or release check below.
- Use `npm ci` and `package-lock.json` for frontend dependencies, and keep
  `src-tauri/Cargo.lock` for the application. Do not introduce a second package
  manager lockfile or update dependencies as part of unrelated cleanup.
- Keep application source and the canonical planning documents tracked. Tauri's
  `src-tauri/gen/schemas/` is generated by the build and stays local, as do test
  runtime data, screenshots, credentials, signing private keys and build outputs.
- Keep source line endings governed by `.gitattributes`; avoid unrelated
  whole-tree normalization when recording a feature checkpoint.
- Rust formatting is checked through the same canonical runner (`cargo fmt
  --check`), alongside TypeScript compilation, tests and diff hygiene. Use
  `.editorconfig` and `.gitattributes` for editor/line-ending consistency. Do not
  silence warnings, weaken assertions or add a second test framework to pass CI.
- PR titles use `type(scope): summary` (scope optional): `feat`, `fix`, `docs`,
  `refactor`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `perf`, or `revert`. Mark unfinished
  changes as draft. Keep intermediate commits useful without forcing a rewrite.
- Use `.github/pull_request_template.md` to record purpose, verification,
  compatibility/recovery risks and reviewer findings. Review naming, module
  boundaries, reuse, duplication, obsolete paths and sensitive/generated files;
  tests do not replace this review. AI review is supplementary, not human approval.
- Squash short-lived feature PRs into `main`, using the reviewed PR title as the
  final commit subject. A development merge is not a release; publishing tags or
  installers still requires explicit authorization. Do not enable automatic merging.
- The merge checks are `Windows full verification`, `Windows desktop smoke test`
  and `PR policy`. The desktop check requires two independent Windows jobs.
  `Windows desktop smoke` sends one scripted message and verifies the same reply
  after reload. `Windows desktop journey` exercises the longer workflows with
  their own fixtures and reports each phase by name. Open the failed job for its
  screenshot and diagnostic JSON. The policy check handles title edits without
  rerunning Windows builds.
  Windows jobs also run for draft PRs on open, code update and reopen. Becoming
  ready for review changes no source input, so only the metadata policy reruns;
  it does not replace, bypass or remove any required check.
  Setup fetches locked dependencies; test execution is offline and isolated.
  Never use `pull_request_target`, repository secrets or a self-hosted desktop
  runner to execute contributor code.
- One maintainer cannot approve their own PR: use zero mandatory approvals until
  another eligible reviewer joins, while still requiring explicit maintainer
  review/merge and resolved conversations. Do not require all-tree CODEOWNERS.
- The public repository's active `Integration PR gates` ruleset protects `main`:
  require PRs and resolved conversations, block force pushes/deletions, and leave
  bypass actors empty. GitHub settings are remote, not enabled by these files.
  During bootstrap, attach the three required checks with their observed GitHub
  Actions app IDs after their first successful runs in the new repository. Require
  an up-to-date base; verify all three requirements by reading the ruleset back.
  Do not claim a required-check gate from a workflow file alone. Keep one ruleset,
  not overlapping classic protections. Reference: `PR-WORKFLOW-REFERENCE.md`.
  The branch rename retained the same ruleset and three required checks; its
  `refs/heads/main` condition and active enforcement were read back after retargeting.
- Local automatic post-commit pushing is disabled. The previous hook is retained
  at `.git/hooks/post-commit.autopush-disabled` for recovery, not execution. Hooks
  are local metadata: inspect existing hooks before each first commit in a checkout;
  do not install automatic pushes in clones.
- The migration checkout has a local `.git/hooks/pre-push` guard requiring the
  clean public root to be the sole ancestry root. It rejects shallow/grafted
  ancestry and ignores replacement refs. This prevents accidental old-history
  pushes, including merges with an unchanged current tree; it does not scan file
  contents or tag messages and is not enforcement in other clones. Never bypass
  it to publish archive refs. Review any cherry-picked content independently.
- Before cleaning historical references, save and verify a local Git bundle.
  Prune only registrations whose worktree directories no longer exist, and
  delete only inactive branches already merged into the current integration
  branch. Leave existing worktrees, unmerged branches and stashes intact; their
  owning runtime must finish its own lifecycle cleanup.
- A development checkpoint is not a release. Record real-window/model and
  installer acceptance gaps in `docs/current-roadmap.md`; do not create a `v*`
  release tag or push any remote without an explicit release/push request.

### Publication boundary

The owner chose MIT and explicitly approved a new public repository with clean
history. On 2026-10-08, the predecessor was renamed to
`shuimo233/AngelBot-private-archive-20261007` and kept private and archived. A
different repository was created at `shuimo233/AngelBot`; only the verified source
tree was bootstrapped, with root `913ce8883891c6954a62e5c6c153547a4280587c` and no
old parent. This is not a force-push followed by publishing the predecessor.

The original history remains in the private archive and a verified local bundle;
old local branches/stash and the runtime-owned worktree were preserved. Do not
push `archive/*`, the stash or runtime branches to the public remote, use
`push --all`/`--mirror`, or merge predecessor history into public branches. A fresh
public clone contains only the new history. Source checks found no confirmed live
credential, but a bounded scan is not an exhaustive no-secrets guarantee. Keep
private recovery material outside published trees and release artifacts.

## One-time repository setup

This setup is for the existing updater-enabled release workflow, not a general
prerequisite for publishing an unsigned early pre-release. The workflow still
requires its updater configuration; this document does not change that workflow
or add an unsigned publishing path.

1. Generate the updater key pair on a trusted machine:

   ```powershell
   npm run tauri -- signer generate --write-keys "$env:USERPROFILE\.tauri\angelbot-updater.key"
   ```

2. Store the private key contents in the GitHub Actions secret
   `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`.
3. If the key has a password, store it in
   `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`.
4. Store the public key contents in the GitHub repository variable
   `TAURI_UPDATER_PUBLIC_KEY`.

Never commit either key or the generated `src-tauri/tauri.release.conf.json`.
The release workflow writes that config from the public key at runtime.

The updater signature proves that an update came from AngelBot. Windows
Authenticode signing is separate: an unsigned early installer may be published
with that limitation disclosed, but must not be described as Windows-signed or
warning-free. Updater signing is still required when distributing updater artifacts.

## Release procedure

### Early pre-release

1. Keep version metadata aligned and put the complete candidate source into an
   explicit reviewed commit under the normal PR/check rules before tagging it.
   Do not tag an old HEAD while the built candidate exists only as uncommitted
   changes. Reuse passing `full`, scoped native and build evidence while their
   inputs and acceptance conditions remain unchanged.
   Code changes still require the affected checks; do not delete tests or weaken
   assertions to publish sooner.
2. Review the actual changes and artifact contents. Known data-loss, unauthorized
   action or unsafe replay defects must be resolved; an unchecked manual item is
   not itself a confirmed defect or a reason to create a VM.
3. Disclose unsigned status, installer checks not performed, supported scope and
   known limitations in the release notes. An early release does not claim clean
   installation, general computer control or natural multi-day reliability.
4. With explicit owner authorization, manually create a draft GitHub release
   from that candidate commit using a non-`v*` tag such as `preview-0.2.0`, upload
   the verified local NSIS and release notes, then publish as **Pre-release**, not
   Latest. The preview tag is release metadata, not a change to the app version.
   Do not upload updater signatures or `latest.json` for this no-updater build.

The existing `release.yml` runs for `v*` tags, requires updater private/public keys,
enables `production-updater` and sets `prerelease: false`. Keep it for the later
stable/updater route; do not use a `v*` tag for the manual early route or weaken
its checks. This distinction does not waive source PR checks or authorize a tag,
push or release by itself; no new workflow or channel framework is needed.

The [beta checklist](../docs/desktop-beta-checklist.md) remains a manual and
extended-acceptance inventory, not an all-items gate for this early stage.

### Stable promotion and updater-enabled releases

Close the checks relevant to the stable release's advertised capabilities in
[the unified roadmap](../docs/current-roadmap.md). `release:check` and a successful
build do not prove runtime-directory alignment, data preservation, uninstall
behavior or clean-account installation. Do not run a quarantined artifact or
label an unperformed check as passed.

1. Update the same SemVer version in `package.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, and
   `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`.
2. Run the following when current, matching evidence is not already available:

   ```powershell
   python scripts/verify.py full
   python scripts/desktop_e2e.py --suite smoke
   python scripts/desktop_e2e.py --suite journey
   npm run release:build
   ```

3. Smoke-test the locally produced NSIS installer in
   `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`.
4. Create and push the matching tag, for example `v0.1.0`. The release
   preflight rejects tags that do not match the application version.
5. With the updater workflow configured, GitHub Actions creates a draft release containing the NSIS installer, signatures,
   and `latest.json`. Install the draft artifacts on a clean Windows account
   and verify launch, first-run setup, project creation, and update behavior.
6. Promote the draft to stable only after the applicable smoke test passes. Draft releases are not
   served by the `releases/latest/download/latest.json` updater endpoint.

## Recovery

For changes to profile cutover or encrypted model storage, explicitly run
`python scripts/verify.py native-storage` on Windows. This exercises the real
credential manager through the production store, using only a unique fixture
namespace, temporary files and one owned child process; it removes its test
keys. It does not use an owner account, window, model or network. It is excluded
from `quick`, `backend`, `full` and default CI; their offline contract is unchanged.
This proves synthetic vault persistence, not owner OAuth renewal or installation.

Normal Windows builds use `%LOCALAPPDATA%\com.angelbot.desktop` for owned
profile data, separate from the per-user `AngelBot` program directory. Before
startup recovery or scheduling, the storage owner locks both old and new roots,
stages the known legacy data and configuration, checks SQLite/WAL, and preserves
the original encrypted credential binding. It does not move project directories,
unknown files or active delegated worktrees. Do not manually merge the roots or
copy a ChatGPT credential file without its binding header.
Manual acceptance borrowing a pre-migration account keeps legacy-compatible
credential writes; borrowing alone does not convert the owner's record format.

After closing all AngelBot and manual acceptance clients, the **new** executable
supports `--rollback-storage` to restore an unchanged cutover and exit without
starting tasks. A normal subsequent launch stays on that recovered profile;
`--migrate-storage` explicitly retries the migration. Do not pass both flags.
Interrupted rollback resumes before startup. If new data, old data or a backup
has changed, recovery refuses to overwrite it; retain both roots and use an
explicit backup/recovery plan instead. This is not automatic downgrade support
or a guarantee against power loss or disk corruption.

Reconnect the official browser service after migration to discover its updated
tool contract. Only its recognized output-directory field is rewritten;
detected legacy absolute arguments suspend custom services. Review custom
commands, environment variables and script-internal paths separately before
enabling them. Migration does not start services or replay previous tool calls.
Do not select the installer's **delete application data** option to troubleshoot
a migration: the retained migration backup is inside the new data directory.

Do not silently downgrade an installed application. If a draft is broken,
delete or replace it before publishing. If a published build is broken, mark
it as non-latest and ship a higher patch version containing the fix. Keep the
previous installers available for manual recovery until the patch is proven.
